DAVIDSON DAY SCHOOL
SEGMENT 2 OF 7
Inside Davidson Day College Support THE ACADEMIC CASE
THE ACADEMIC CASE
Rigor & Credentials
A rigorous, weighted, no-rank transcript — presented to colleges through a detailed profile, with
several credential figures the school chooses not to publish.
A note on how to read this dossier. Where Davidson Day does not publish a figure, we say so plainly
and mark it a transparency gap. An unpublished number is a gap in what the school discloses — it is
never, on its own, a verdict that the school is weak at college support. We report only what the school
publishes and what independent research surfaced.
How the transcript is built and explained
Davidson Day gives college readers a clear framework for reading a Patriot transcript, even without test
scores or class rank. Honors courses are weighted +0.5 and Advanced Placement courses +1.0; the
post-AP Calculus III also carries a full extra point. Grade-point averages reflect only courses taken at
Davidson Day — transfer courses, online courses, independent studies, and Upper School courses taken
during Middle School are excluded. When a student transfers in with outside credits, the prior school's
transcript is enclosed alongside the Davidson Day transcript.
Davidson Day does not rank its students. In place of rank, the School Profile publishes the Class of 2026
grade-point distribution, which gives colleges context for any single student's standing:
4.60 3.96 2.49 No rank
Highest GPA (Class of 2026) Median GPA (Class of 2026) Lowest GPA (Class of 2026) Class-rank policy
The published grading scale, weighting rules, GPA distribution, and honor code together do the work that a
class rank would otherwise do — they let an admissions reader place a student in context. (The whole-class
implications of the no-rank policy are taken up in Segment 7.)
A broad Advanced Placement catalog
The School Profile lists AP offerings across English, Mathematics, Science, History, World Language,
Technology, and the Arts — including Calculus AB and BC, Statistics, the sciences, several histories and
social sciences, Spanish and French language, Computer Science Principles and Computer Science A, and
Studio Art. For students who exhaust the sequence, the school offers Calculus III (Post-AP) and
Independent Studies, and international-research students earn additional academic credit through the
programs detailed in Segment 5.
Davidson Day School · College Support Series · Parent-facing dossier Page 1
DAVIDSON DAY SCHOOL
SEGMENT 2 OF 7
Inside Davidson Day College Support THE ACADEMIC CASE
TRANSPARENCY GAP — AP exam pass rates are not published
The profile documents the AP catalog, but Davidson Day does not publish AP exam pass rates (the share of
exams scored 3 or higher). This is a common independent-school disclosure choice. Offerings tell you what a
student can take; they do not, by themselves, establish exam outcomes — and the absence of the figure is a
transparency gap, not evidence of weak results.
Testing & National Merit
Two of the credential figures parents most often look for are, by the school's own choice or by absence of
public record, not available here.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — SAT / ACT profiles are deliberately withheld
The School Profile states plainly: “Due to the popularity of test-optional policies, we will not be providing the
testing profiles for the Class of 2026.” This is a deliberate transparency choice tied to test-optional admissions
— not a signal about how students score. Self-reported score ranges appear on some third-party aggregators,
but those are user-submitted, not school-reported, and do not close this gap; we do not substitute them.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — National Merit standing is unpublished / unconfirmed
No National Merit semifinalist or commended-scholar data for Davidson Day School (Davidson, NC) could be
located in National Merit Scholarship Corporation materials or local press. Searches surfaced only similarly
named institutions — most notably Davidson Academy in Reno, Nevada, whose National Merit counts and test
scores are a different school's and must never be attributed to Davidson Day. Treat Davidson Day's National
Merit standing as unpublished/unconfirmed.
Pronunciation notes for the audio episode: “A.P.” for Advanced Placement; “SAT” and “ACT” as the familiar test names.
Davidson Day School · College Support Series · Parent-facing dossier Page 2

DAVIDSON DAY SCHOOL
SEGMENT 4 OF 7
Inside Davidson Day College Support APPLICATION SUPPORT
APPLICATION SUPPORT
The Application Itself
Structured, student-owned support across the list, the essay, and financial aid — with several
process specifics the public record does not confirm.
A note on how to read this dossier. Where Davidson Day does not publish a figure, we say so plainly
and mark it a transparency gap. An unpublished number is a gap in what the school discloses — it is
never, on its own, a verdict that the school is weak at college support. We report only what the school
publishes and what independent research surfaced.
What the office does
The college-counseling office assists students with building a balanced college list, writing the application
essay, navigating the financial-aid process, and planning for careers — while emphasizing that students
retain ultimate responsibility for their own applications. Application materials are submitted through Scoir.
The fall Senior Application Boot Camp and the spring Financial Aid Night and Athletic Recruitment
Workshop (Segment 1) are the scheduled anchors of this support.
The merit-aid track record
The clearest published outcome of the school's application support is scholarship dollars offered:
$7.4M+ 53 100% 11
Merit awards offered (Class of Matriculated to a 4-year
Graduates in the class NCAA student-athletes
2025) college
The Class of 2025's 53 members were offered more than $7.4 million in merit awards. That is a strong
aggregate for a class this size; the school does not, however, publish the breadth of merit across the class
(how many students received awards, or typical award size), so the $7.4 million total is the figure to rely on.
Where the public record runs out
Several mechanics that families reasonably ask about are simply not documented in the school's public
materials. We flag them as unconfirmed rather than guess — they are good questions to put directly to the
office.
Davidson Day School · College Support Series · Parent-facing dossier Page 1
DAVIDSON DAY SCHOOL
SEGMENT 4 OF 7
Inside Davidson Day College Support APPLICATION SUPPORT
TRANSPARENCY GAP — “Is every application reviewed before submission?”
We could not confirm from Davidson Day's own materials a stated policy that every application is reviewed
before submission, nor a formalized letter-of-recommendation management protocol beyond Scoir submission.
Many small offices do review; the point is that Davidson Day does not publish the commitment, so we do not
assert it.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — Early Decision / Early Action doctrine
The office covers standardized-test planning and list strategy, but a specific published ED/EA strategy for
Davidson Day was not located. Whether the office steers toward, or away from, binding Early Decision in
particular cases is not documented.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — FAFSA / CSS Profile navigation — and a caution about “Clarity”
Financial Aid Night is an annual event, but detailed FAFSA/CSS Profile navigation content for the college aid
process was not located on the school's site. Note one easy point of confusion: Davidson Day uses a tool called
Clarity for its own tuition-assistance process — that is the school's admission aid, not college FAFSA/CSS help.
Treat detailed college financial-aid navigation as unconfirmed.
Help securing internships or jobs for upperclassmen is addressed less through the counseling office directly
and more through the structured Diploma Distinctions — the Business & Civic Engagement and STEMM
tracks each require a 100-hour practicum (detailed in Segment 5).
Davidson Day School · College Support Series · Parent-facing dossier Page 2

DAVIDSON DAY SCHOOL
SEGMENT 1 OF 7
Inside Davidson Day College Support THE COUNSELING ENGINE
THE COUNSELING ENGINE
People, Timing & Tools
A two-person, high-touch office that starts in 9th grade — anchored by a director with real
university-admissions experience.
A note on how to read this dossier. Where Davidson Day does not publish a figure, we say so plainly
and mark it a transparency gap. An unpublished number is a gap in what the school discloses — it is
never, on its own, a verdict that the school is weak at college support. We report only what the school
publishes and what independent research surfaced.
The office at a glance
Davidson Day runs a small, relationship-driven college-counseling office. Its competitive edge comes less
from published test or scholarship metrics — most of which the school does not disclose — and more from
institutional design: an early start, a favorable caseload, a director with genuine admissions-office
experience, and signature research programs (covered in Segment 5) that give students a distinctive
application narrative.
2 ~99:1 9th ~71
Upper School students per Grade individualized College reps hosted (recent
College counselors (by role)
counselor counseling begins fall)
The office is staffed by two people — a Director of College Counseling and an Associate Director of College
Counseling — supported by a Registrar who handles transcript functions. (Consistent with series practice,
individuals are referenced by role only.)
Backgrounds & stability
The Director is a former university admissions officer. Before moving into secondary-school counseling,
she served roughly 2007–2013 as a senior assistant director of admissions at a selective private university,
and holds a master's in counselor education and a bachelor's in psychology. This is the single most relevant
credential to the common parent question — “has anyone here sat on the other side of the desk?” — and the
answer is yes. She has been at Davidson Day since 2013 (about twelve to thirteen years), essentially her
entire post-university career, including a brief interim Head of Upper School assignment in 2023–24. That
reflects high staff stability.
The Associate Director's verifiable background is in athletics and school administration, and she progressed
internally from a college-counseling associate role into the associate-director position. Public records do not
show a university admissions-officer role for her, and no graduate degree could be independently confirmed
— so we make no claim either way. She is a confirmed member of the Southern Association for College
Davidson Day School · College Support Series · Parent-facing dossier Page 1
DAVIDSON DAY SCHOOL
SEGMENT 1 OF 7
Inside Davidson Day College Support THE COUNSELING ENGINE
Admission Counseling.
Caseload
Two counselors serve an Upper School of 198 students — roughly 99 students per counselor across grades
9–12, and about 23–24 seniors per counselor in the roughly 47-student Class of 2026. Against public-school
norms, where counselor caseloads in the several-hundreds are common, these are small, favorable ratios
that make the school's “individualized, student-centered” description credible.
When it begins & the tools families use
Individualized, student-centered college counseling begins in 9th grade, per the school's own materials —
not junior year. The office runs its process and its college-rep visit scheduling through Scoir (pronounced
“score”), a platform that gives families college-list management with acceptance-likelihood categorization
and financial-aid estimates.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — Do families receive outcome scattergrams?
We could not confirm from Davidson Day's own materials whether families are specifically given
admission-outcome scattergrams (the GPA/test-score scatter plots some schools surface through their
platform). Scoir can support such tools, but the school does not document providing them. Families should ask
the office directly. Unpublished here means unconfirmed — not absent.
A published-events backbone
The office runs a full, predictable slate of programming that keeps families informed at each stage:
• Fall: Senior Night, Junior Planning Night, College 101, and a Senior Application Boot Camp.
• Spring: Financial Aid Night, an Athletic Recruitment Workshop, a Case Studies program, and
Freshman & Sophomore Planning Night.
Professional memberships include NACAC and SACAC (the national and regional admission-counseling
associations) and ACCIS (the Association of College Counselors in Independent Schools), alongside the
school's SAIS, NAIS, and College Board affiliations.
Pronunciation note for the audio episode: Scoir is said “score” — it is never spelled out letter by letter.
Davidson Day School · College Support Series · Parent-facing dossier Page 2

sections.text:
DAVIDSON DAY SCHOOL
SEGMENT 7 OF 7
Inside Davidson Day College Support FIT & THE WHOLE CLASS
FIT, RANK & THE WHOLE CLASS
Best Fit Over Prestige
A no-rank, individualized philosophy that aims to serve every student — with a learning-support
center whose application-stage role isn't fully documented.
A note on how to read this dossier. Where Davidson Day does not publish a figure, we say so plainly
and mark it a transparency gap. An unpublished number is a gap in what the school discloses — it is
never, on its own, a verdict that the school is weak at college support. We report only what the school
publishes and what independent research surfaced.
No rank — by design
Davidson Day does not rank its students, and it says so directly to colleges. Instead of a rank, the School
Profile publishes the Class of 2026 GPA distribution (highest 4.60, median 3.96, lowest 2.49; see Segment
2), which lets an admissions reader understand where a student sits without reducing the class to an ordinal
list. The effect is to protect students in the middle of a small class from being defined by a rank number — a
philosophy choice as much as a data choice.
A best-fit, whole-class philosophy
The office describes its counseling as “individualized and student-centered,” oriented toward the best-fit
college rather than the most prestigious name. The spring Case Studies Program reinforces this by teaching
families to see admissions as a question of institutional fit — what a given college is trying to build in its
class — rather than a pure ranking of applicant merit. That framing is designed to serve the whole class:
students aiming at the most selective schools, students who are strong but not at the very top, and students
changing direction late.
Learning support: the Learning Enrichment Center
Davidson Day's Learning Enrichment Center (LEC) is a genuine, staffed support structure — not just an
accommodations desk. It provides one-on-one tutoring, academic coaching and executive-function support,
social-skills groups, speech-language therapy, and occupational therapy, serving students from age two
through grade twelve, and it coordinates with classroom teachers. For families whose child learns differently,
that continuity of support through the Upper School years is a real asset in keeping a college-bound
trajectory intact.
Davidson Day School · College Support Series · Parent-facing dossier Page 1
DAVIDSON DAY SCHOOL
SEGMENT 7 OF 7
Inside Davidson Day College Support FIT & THE WHOLE CLASS
TRANSPARENCY GAP — The LEC's application-stage role isn't separately documented
What we could not confirm is the LEC's specific role during the college-application stage — for instance, how it
helps document approved accommodations so they carry over to college testing and campus disability
services. The learning support is well documented; its hand-off into the application process is not. Families
relying on accommodations should ask the LEC and the counseling office how that coordination works.
The through-line
Taken together, the no-rank policy, the fit-first counseling stance, and a learning-support center that runs the
length of a student's time at the school describe an office built to serve a range of students rather than only
its highest achievers. Where the school publishes less — the exact mechanics of supporting students who
are struggling or pivoting late — we have said so rather than fill the space; the documented philosophy is
clear, even where the documented process is thin.
Davidson Day School · College Support Series · Parent-facing dossier Page 2

---

sections.text:
DAVIDSON DAY SCHOOL
SEGMENT 3 OF 7
Inside Davidson Day College Support INSTITUTIONAL LEVERAGE
INSTITUTIONAL LEVERAGE
How the School's Name Works for Your
Child
Leverage here is built through access and context — a heavy rep-visit calendar, a regional
case-studies program, and a profile document that frames each student.
A note on how to read this dossier. Where Davidson Day does not publish a figure, we say so plainly
and mark it a transparency gap. An unpublished number is a gap in what the school discloses — it is
never, on its own, a verdict that the school is weak at college support. We report only what the school
publishes and what independent research surfaced.
Admissions officers come to campus
Davidson Day's leverage is expressed less through formal named partnerships and more through sustained
access — bringing admissions officers to the students, and sending counselors to campuses. The school
schedules visits, Monday through Friday throughout the fall, through Scoir, and students get direct
conversation time with visiting representatives.
A note on the numbers — “80+” vs. the documented count
The College Counseling page advertises welcoming “more than 80 college admission representatives” each
year — the school's standing benchmark. Its most recent specific reporting, however, documents 71
representatives in a recent fall, with nearly 80% visiting from out-of-state institutions. Both are worth stating
honestly: “80+” is the marketing benchmark; ~71 (heavily out-of-state) is the documented recent figure.
A regional case-studies program & college fair
Each spring Davidson Day co-hosts — with a neighboring independent school — a Lake Norman-area
College Admissions Case Studies Program and College Fair. Families work through real (fictionalized)
application files for a mock institution, seeing an admissions committee's decision-making from the inside. At
the prior event, per the school, the gym “transformed into a vibrant college fair with nearly 70 colleges and
universities represented.” It is a concrete way the school demystifies selective admissions for its families.
The School Profile as a contextualizing document
The single most valuable lever Davidson Day controls is its published School Profile — the document
colleges receive alongside every transcript. It explains the no-rank policy, the GPA weighting and grading
scale, the Class of 2026 GPA distribution, the curriculum's rigor, the honor code, and the school's signature
programs. In other words, it does the work of framing each student for an admissions reader who has never
Davidson Day School · College Support Series · Parent-facing dossier Page 1
DAVIDSON DAY SCHOOL
SEGMENT 3 OF 7
Inside Davidson Day College Support INSTITUTIONAL LEVERAGE
visited Davidson, North Carolina — and it does so without leaning on test scores or rank.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — No published roster of formal “named relationships”
Beyond its association memberships (NACAC, SACAC, ACCIS, College Board, SAIS, NAIS) and the
neighboring-school case-studies partnership, we did not find a published list of formal, named relationships with
specific college admissions offices. The leverage is real but is expressed through rep visits and counselor
campus visits rather than through advertised institutional partnerships — so we describe it that way rather than
imply a pipeline that isn't documented.
Davidson Day School · College Support Series · Parent-facing dossier Page 2

sections.text:
DAVIDSON DAY SCHOOL
SEGMENT 5 OF 7
Inside Davidson Day College Support STANDING OUT
STANDING OUT
The Signature Strength
Davidson Day's distinctive hook: genuine, credited international field research and structured
Diploma Distinctions that hand students a story no test score can tell.
A note on how to read this dossier. Where Davidson Day does not publish a figure, we say so plainly
and mark it a transparency gap. An unpublished number is a gap in what the school discloses — it is
never, on its own, a verdict that the school is weak at college support. We report only what the school
publishes and what independent research surfaced.
The hook engine: international archaeological research
For a school this size, the standout differentiator is unusually concrete. Through its AFAR program
(American Foreign Academic Research), Davidson Day students do real, full-scale archaeological field
research abroad — not tourism, but excavation and analysis that has fed peer-reviewed scholarship. Per the
2025–26 School Profile, students have conducted research in Belize since 2009, Spain since 2014,
Greece since 2017, and Portugal since 2018, with fieldwork including the Tróia site in Portugal and a
domestic project at the Adam Spach Rock House in North Carolina.
Two dates are worth stating cleanly so neither reads as an error: AFAR founded its first U.S. high-school
archaeological field school in 2006, at Cahal Pech in Belize; Davidson Day's own profile documents the
school's full-scale research program as running since 2009. The Belize excavation is conducted jointly with
the Belize Valley Archaeological Reconnaissance project, under permit from the Belize Institute of
Archaeology. The program was founded and is led by a Davidson Day faculty member, who also directs the
Global Studies Diploma (referenced by role, per series practice).
Participation counts — cite the source, don't round
How many students have taken part depends on the source and the window. The program's own site
(goafar.org) describes “hundreds” of high-school students since 2007; a peer-reviewed 2020 history in the
journal Heritage reports “more than 200 high-school students since 2010.” Both are legitimate; we cite them
specifically rather than inventing a single round number.
The academic payoff is visible: AFAR students have presented their work at collegiate research conferences
— for example, roughly ten Davidson Day students presenting summer research on Belize, Portugal, and
Spain at a university archaeology conference, nine of whom were also Global Studies Diploma candidates.
That is exactly the kind of credential that reads as distinctive in a selective-admissions file.
Diploma Distinctions: a structured way to stand out
Davidson Day School · College Support Series · Parent-facing dossier Page 1
DAVIDSON DAY SCHOOL
SEGMENT 5 OF 7
Inside Davidson Day College Support STANDING OUT
Davidson Day offers three formal Diploma Distinctions that students apply to at the end of sophomore year.
They convert interest into a documented, multi-year credential.
Global Studies Diploma
• Undertaken by more than a quarter of the student body — a notably broad reach for a signature
program.
• Requires four years of the same world language, at least two weeks of international field research, and
a capstone paper.
• Produces a separate transcript and profile sent to colleges alongside the standard record. In place
since 2021.
STEMM and Business & Civic Engagement Diplomas
• Structured advanced coursework (AP/Honors) in the relevant field, plus a 100-hour practicum.
• Quarterly Ethics Labs; an 11th-grade Research Methods Honors course; a 12th-grade Capstone
Research Honors mentorship.
• Capstones are presented at the Davidson Day Scholars Research Conference — a public,
documented research showcase.
Arts portfolios & athletic recruiting
For artists, Davidson Day offers AP Studio Art and supports portfolio development aimed at competitive
art-and-design programs (the kind of schools — SCAD, RISD, Chapman — that evaluate a portfolio). For
athletes, the office runs an annual Athletic Recruitment Workshop and stages National Signing Day events
(one recent November day saw seven National Letter of Intent signings). The school reports that more than
100 Davidson Day student-athletes have gone on to compete at over 80 colleges, and the counseling
page links NCAA eligibility resources.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — Portfolio advising is a program, not a documented counseling protocol
The art program supports portfolio building, but we did not find a documented, counseling-office-level protocol
for guiding fine-arts portfolio applicants through the distinct application process (supplements, portfolio review
days, art-school-specific financial aid). Families of prospective art-school applicants should ask how that
hand-off works.

“TROY-uh.”
